title: Peterborough paranormal investigator explores 40 years of ghost encounters in new book

content:
After four decades of investigating things that go bump in the night, a Peterborough paranormal researcher is sharing his experiences in a new book that explores the mysteries of ghosts, spirits and unexplained phenomena.

Canadian paranormal investigator Cameron Bagg has released his first non-fiction book, Ghost Revelations: Adventures of a Technical Medium, drawing on more than 40 years of research and over 1,000 investigations.

The book examines some of the most influential cases of Bagg’s career, including encounters he believes provide evidence of paranormal activity.

Through personal accounts, photographs and discussions of specialized equipment, Bagg hopes to convince readers that ghosts are real.

While traditional ghost sightings are a major focus, the book also explores a wide range of unexplained phenomena.

Bagg discusses reported encounters with spirits, shadow beings and mysterious orbs, along with creatures associated with cryptozoology, including the Dover Demon, Dogman and Sabe.

The author examines how these reported entities might fit within what he describes as a paranormal spectrum of consciousness.

A central feature of the book is its collection of photographs, which Bagg presents as evidence supporting his investigations.

He also outlines techniques involving digital cameras that he believes can be used to capture images of spirits in locations that are not traditionally considered haunted.

Those claims remain scientifically unverified, but Bagg hopes his research will encourage readers to reconsider conventional ideas about paranormal activity.

Bagg says the goal of Ghost Revelations is to offer new perspectives on mysteries that have fascinated people for generations.

The book combines his personal experiences with an examination of the technical tools he believes are useful for paranormal investigations.

Ghost Revelations: Adventures of a Technical Medium is now available through Amazon, Kindle and select bookstores.

Bagg also plans to attend book expos and paranormal conventions across Ontario this fall, where he hopes to connect with readers and others interested in unexplained phenomena.
